items.followUp: Define acceleration due to gravity and state its approximate value on Earth in SI units.

rubric.why: Awards the definition of gravitational acceleration.
rubric.how: Check that the answer identifies the acceleration of a freely falling body due to gravity.

rubric.why: Awards the approximate value and its SI unit.
rubric.description: Gives the value of gravitational acceleration in SI units.

modelAnswer: Gravitational acceleration is the acceleration of a freely falling body due to the force of gravity.
Its value near the Earth’s surface is g = 9.8 m s⁻².

items.followUp: Define the pivot and a deformable body.

rubric.why: Awards the definition of moment arm.
rubric.how: Check that it is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of a force.

rubric.why: Awards the defining property of a rigid body.
rubric.how: Check that the distances between any two particles in the body remain unchanged.

modelAnswer: The moment arm is the perpendicular distance between the pivot and the line of action of a force.
A rigid body is a body in which the distance between any two particles remains unchanged.

items.followUp: What is an ideal machine? State its efficiency.

rubric.why: Awards the defining feature of an ideal system.
rubric.how: Check that it has no energy loss or that output work equals input work.

rubric.why: Awards the efficiency of an ideal system.

modelAnswer: An ideal system is a system in which there is no loss of energy, so output work equals input work.

items.followUp: Define one joule of work in terms of power and time.

rubric.why: Awards identification of the watt as the unit of power.
rubric.how: Check that the watt is identified as the SI unit of power.

rubric.why: Awards the operational definition of one watt.
rubric.how: Check that one watt is defined as one joule of work done in one second, or as 1 J s⁻¹.

modelAnswer: The watt (W) is the SI unit of power.
One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second: 1 W = 1 J s⁻¹.

items.followUp: Define significant figures and state two rules for identifying them.

rubric.why: Awards the definition of significant figures.
rubric.how: Check that the definition includes the accurately known digits and the first doubtful or estimated digit.

rubric.why: Awards a valid rule for identifying significant figures.
rubric.description: States the rule for zeros between non-zero digits.
rubric.how: Check that zeros between non-zero digits are counted as significant.

rubric.why: Awards a second valid rule for identifying significant figures.
rubric.description: States the rule for leading zeros.
rubric.how: Check that leading zeros are not counted as significant.

modelAnswer: Significant figures are the accurately known digits in a measurement together with the first doubtful or estimated digit.
Zeros between non-zero digits are significant.

items.followUp: A car travels at a uniform speed of 72 km h⁻¹ for 15 s. Find the distance it travels.

rubric.why: Awards the given data expressed in SI units.
rubric.description: Writes the given data in SI units.
rubric.how: Check that 36 km h⁻¹ is converted to 10 m s⁻¹ and the time is stated as 10 s.

rubric.why: Awards the correct relationship for uniform motion.
rubric.how: Check that distance is calculated as velocity multiplied by time.

rubric.why: Awards correct substitution of the SI values.
rubric.description: Substitutes the SI values into the formula.
rubric.how: Check that 10 m s⁻¹ and 10 s are substituted into the distance formula.

rubric.why: Awards the calculated distance with its unit.
rubric.how: Check for a final distance of 100 m.

modelAnswer: Given: v = 36 km h⁻¹ = 10 m s⁻¹, t = 10 s.

items.followUp: State and explain the second condition of equilibrium.

rubric.why: Awards the statement of the first condition of equilibrium.
rubric.description: States the first condition of equilibrium.
rubric.how: Check that the vector sum or resultant of all forces acting on the body is zero.

rubric.why: Awards an explanation of how the forces balance.
rubric.how: Check that forces in one direction are balanced by equal forces in the opposite direction.

rubric.why: Awards the mathematical expression of the condition.

modelAnswer: The first condition of equilibrium is that the resultant force acting on a body is zero.
Thus, the forces acting in one direction are balanced by equal forces acting in the opposite direction.
Mathematically, ΣF = 0; in two dimensions, ΣFₓ = 0 and ΣFᵧ = 0.
